bug_semantics: python_sandbox_server's RestrictedPython sandbox in server_fastmcp.py is bypassable because create_safe_globals() exposes CPython's raw getattr/setattr (and hasattr) in safe_builtins, execute() never installs a RestrictedPython _getattr_ guard (only _getiter_/_getitem_), and the builtins merge does merged_builtins.update(our_builtins) so the raw getattr overwrites RestrictedPython's controlled entries. validate_code() then only substring-matches literal dunders such as '__class__', which a payload can construct at runtime. An attacker who can call the execute_code MCP tool walks the class hierarchy through getattr, reaches subprocess.Popen, and runs OS commands as the server process. HTTP/SSE exposure without auth (added later) raises this to unauthenticated RCE when that transport is enabled; the getattr hole itself is present from first write.
flaw_origin: The getattr sandbox hole was first written in public member cb5cd12a5882b59a8e441e84e636b2b960dc912f ('MCP Servers and Plugins', 2025-09-19) of squash PR #1051, which added mcp-servers/python/python_sandbox_server/src/python_sandbox_server/server_fastmcp.py as a new file. Line 181 maps 'getattr': getattr and 'setattr': setattr into safe_builtins; lines 292-295 reject only literal dunder substrings; lines 416-428 merge builtins without injecting _getattr_. Immediate parent 7af39689f6d99b6659f064bd7bba78b7025279e1 has no python_sandbox_server tree and no RestrictedPython getattr mapping. Later PR members only reformat/headers/chmod; HTTP transport arrives later in 7105ee0cb14c4faa3e202b895bdc52bf3a083121 and does not change getattr.

The causal hole is the first write of raw getattr in RestrictedPython's execution globals plus substring-only dunder validation and a missing _getattr_ guard. git log --follow --diff-filter=A lands on squash 771ffb8 (#1051). That squash is not the BIC: PR #1051 members are reconstructable in the clone and on GitHub.
